exposure: pathogenic deletion encompassing 2.0 Kb of 7P15.3 (exons 64 and 65 of DNAH11)
cohort: Monochorionic diamniotic newborn twins suspected of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD).
finding: The study identified a novel compound heterozygous mutation (c.2436C > G and a pathogenic deletion encompassing exons 64 and 65) in the DNAH11 gene in the newborn twins with PCD.
